cards.back:
The answer to a division.
The quotient of 20 divided by 4 is 5.
cards.say: Quotient. The answer to a division. The quotient of twenty divided by four is five.

cards.back:
The answer to a multiplication.
The product of 6 and 7 is 42.
cards.say: Product. The answer to a multiplication. The product of six and seven is forty two.

cards.back:
The answer to an addition.
The sum of 250 and 130 is 380.
cards.say: Sum. The answer to an addition. The sum of two hundred and fifty and one hundred and thirty is three hundred and eighty.

cards.back: How much bigger one number is than another. It is the answer to a subtraction.
cards.say: Difference. How much bigger one number is than another. It is the answer to a subtraction.

cards.back:
What is left over after dividing as far as possible.
23 ÷ 5 is 4 remainder 3.
cards.say: Remainder. What is left over after dividing as far as possible. Twenty three divided by five is four remainder three.

cards.back: The top number of a fraction. It says how many parts we have.
cards.say: Numerator. The top number of a fraction. It says how many parts we have.

cards.back: The bottom number of a fraction. It says how many equal parts make the whole.
cards.say: Denominator. The bottom number of a fraction. It says how many equal parts make the whole.

cards.back:
Fractions that name the same amount.
2/3 and 4/6 are equivalent.
cards.say: Equivalent fractions. Fractions that name the same amount. Two thirds and four sixths are equivalent.

cards.back:
One of 10 equal parts of a whole.
1/10 = 0.1
cards.say: Tenth. One of ten equal parts of a whole. One tenth equals zero point one

cards.back:
One of 100 equal parts of a whole.
1/100 = 0.01
cards.say: Hundredth. One of one hundred equal parts of a whole. One hundredth equals zero point zero one

cards.back:
The dot that separates whole numbers from parts of a whole.
In 3.4 it sits between the 3 and the 4.
cards.say: Decimal point. The dot that separates whole numbers from parts of a whole. In three point four it sits between the three and the four.

cards.back:
The value of a digit depends on its place in the number.
In 5,382 the 3 is worth 300.
cards.say: Place value. The value of a digit depends on its place in the number. In five thousand three hundred and eighty two the three is worth three hundred.

cards.back:
A sensible guess that is close to the exact answer.
We often round the numbers first.
cards.say: Estimate. A sensible guess that is close to the exact answer. We often round the numbers first.

cards.back:
The operation that undoes another one.
Addition and subtraction are inverses. So are multiplication and division.
cards.say: Inverse operation. The operation that undoes another one. Addition and subtraction are inverses. So are multiplication and division.

cards.back:
A number below zero.
A temperature of 3 degrees below zero is written as -3.
cards.say: Negative number. A number below zero. A temperature of three degrees below zero is written as negative three.
Quadrilateral. A polygon with four sides.

cards.back: The distance all the way around the edge of a shape.
cards.say: Perimeter. The distance all the way around the edge of a shape.

cards.back: A line that splits a shape into two halves that are mirror images.
cards.say: Line of symmetry. A line that splits a shape into two halves that are mirror images.
